extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining and making rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 (including provisional 102(e) rejections), selecting/wording form paragraphs, and determining prior art dates for U.S. patents, U.S. application publications, and international applications (PCT).

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(e) prior art date for patents/publications from IAs filed prior to November 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference U.S. patent issued from an international application (IA) that was filed prior to November 29, 2000 has a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date of the date of fulfillment of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1), (2) and (4). The application publications, both the WIPO publication and the U.S. publication, published from an international application that was filed prior to November 29, 2000, do not have any 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to 35 U.S.C. 102(e) and 374 are not applicable to IAs having international filing dates prior to Nov. 29, 2000. Such IA publications can be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of their publication dates. See form paragraph 7.12.01 and Examiner Notes for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(e) prior art date for patents/publications from IAs filed on or after November 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: All references (WIPO publication, U.S. patent application publication, or U.S. patent) of or claiming the benefit of an IA filed on or after Nov. 29, 2000, designated the U.S., and published in English under PCT Article 21(2) have the 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date of the international filing date or earlier effective U.S. filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No benefit of the international filing date (nor any U.S. filing dates prior to the IA) is given for 35 U.S.C. 102(e) purposes if the IA was published by WIPO in a language other than English. Use form paragraph 7.12 and follow Examiner Notes to determine the 102(e) date. Consider benefit/priority claims only if subject matter is appropriately supported in earlier disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: IA publications not published in English or not designating the U.S.: cannot be applied under 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application was published by WIPO in a language other than English, or did not designate the U.S., the IA publication by WIPO (and certain related U.S. publications/patents) may not be applied as a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such references may be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of their publication date. If a U.S. publication or patent issued from a continuing application claiming benefit to such an IA, the 102(e) date may be the earliest U.S. filing date after the IA filing date (see Examiner Notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining 102(e) prior art date: consider benefit/priority claims only with proper support
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date, consider priority/benefit claims to earlier-filed U.S. provisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), U.S. nonprovisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 120 or 121, and international applications under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c) only if the subject matter used to make the rejection is appropriately supported in the relied-upon earlier-filed application's disclosure (and any intermediate application(s)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT consider foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) and 365(a). A benefit claim to a U.S. patent of an earlier-filed international application may only result in an effective U.S. filing date as of the date the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1), (2) and (4) were fulfilled (pre-AIPA situations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pre-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (form paragraph 7.12.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference is a U.S. patent issued directly or indirectly from a national stage of, or a continuing application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 365(c) to, an IA having an international filing date prior to Nov. 29, 2000, apply pre-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (form paragraph 7.12.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prior art date of such a reference is the date the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1), (2) and (4) were fulfilled. Use form paragraph 7.12.01 and associated Examiner Notes to assist determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection for copending U.S. applications (common inventor/assignee)
rubrics_metrics.description: If at least one common inventor exists between the applications or the applications are commonly assigned and the effective filing dates are different, a provisional 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection of the later-filed application should be made when the earlier-filed copending unpublished U.S. application discloses subject matter that would anticipate the later-filed application's claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional because the earlier-filed application is unpublished; it presumes future publication/patenting of the copending application. Use form paragraph 7.15.01 when making such provisional rejections. The provisional rejection may be overcome by a 37 CFR 1.132 derivation showing or a suitable 37 CFR 1.131 showing; it may NOT be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer (In re Bartfeld). If claims would have been obvious over the copending application, give obviousness form paragraph (7.21.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: No provisional 102(e) rejection when copending applications have no common inventor or assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no common assignee or common inventor and the application was not published pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b), the confidential status of applications under 35 U.S.C. 122(a) must be maintained and no rejection can be made relying on the earlier-filed, unpublished application as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing dates are within 6 months of each other (3 months for simple subject matter) an interference may be proper. If the earlier application will not be published under 122(b), it must be allowed to issue once statutory requirements are met; after publication it may be used as a 102(e) reference in the still-pending application as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph use and ordering (7.07 to 7.15 series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.07 through 7.15 and related paragraphs are the standard templates to state statutory basis and to make rejections under the various 35 U.S.C. 102 subsections. The particular part of the reference relied upon should be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 7.07 (Statement of Statutory Basis, 35 U.S.C. 102) should precede many of the paragraphs and is required only in first actions on the merits and final rejections (otherwise use 7.103). Form paragraphs 7.07 to 7.14 are to be used ONLY ONCE in a given Office action. Specific paragraphs (e.g., 7.08, 7.09, 7.10, 7.11, 7.12, 7.12.01, 7.13, 7.14, 7.15, 7.15.01–7.15.03) have their own precedence and Examiner Notes—follow those instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.08 — 102(a) Activity by another before applicant's invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Text of 35 U.S.C. 102(a): (a) the invention was known or used by others in this country, or patented or described in a printed publication in this or a foreign country, before the invention thereof by the applicant for a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.09 — 102(b) activity more than one year prior to filing (statutory bar)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text of 35 U.S.C. 102(b): (b) the invention was patented or described in a printed publication in this or a foreign country or in public use or on sale in this country, more than one year prior to the date of application for patent in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07, and may be preceded by 7.08.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.10 — 102(c) abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Text of 35 U.S.C. 102(c): (c) he has abandoned the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by 7.07 and may be preceded by one or more of 7.08 and 7.09.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.11 — 102(d) foreign patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Text of 35 U.S.C. 102(d): (d) the invention was first patented or caused to be patented ... in a foreign country prior to the date of the application for patent in this country on an application filed more than twelve months before the filing of the application in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by 7.07, and may be preceded by one or more of 7.08 to 7.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.13 — 102(f) applicant not the inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Text of 35 U.S.C. 102(f): (f) he did not himself invent the subject matter sought to be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by 7.07, and may be preceded by one or more of 7.08 to 7.12. See MPEP § 2137–2137.02 for substantive requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.14 — 102(g) priority of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Text of 35 U.S.C. 102(g): priority is determined in interference proceedings considering conception, reduction to practice, and reasonable diligence, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by 7.07, and may be preceded by one or more of 7.08 to 7.13. See MPEP § 2138–2138.06 and Chapter 2300 for interference procedure details.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.15 series — general rejection language and variants for 102(a),(b),(g),(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.15 is a general rejection template: 'Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102[2] as being [3] by [4].' Specific follow-up paragraphs (7.15.02, 7.15.03) cover 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejections where the reference has or does not have a common assignee/inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bracket inserts must be filled appropriately (paragraph letter, 'clearly anticipated' vs 'anticipated' with explanation, prior art relied upon). If 102(e) is applied, follow with 7.15.02 or 7.15.03. 7.15 must be preceded by 7.07 and as appropriate other paragraphs or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph ¶7.15.01 — Provisional rejection template and examiner notes
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.15.01 provides the specific language for a provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) when the reference is a copending application with a common assignee or at least one common inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes wording about presumption of future publication/patenting and lists how the provisional rejection might be overcome (37 CFR 1.132, 1.131). Examiner Notes specify use conditions: common assignee or at least one common inventor, application unpublished, use of form paragraph 7.12/7.12.01 to determine 102(e) date as applicable, interplay with obviousness and double patenting rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: When patent application publications may be used as 102(e) references
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent application publications may only be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) if the appropriate form paragraph (e.g., 7.12) is applicable and was preceded by the statutory statement (7.07) as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the publication meets the statutory and timing requirements (e.g., filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), international application conditions) before using as a 102(e) reference; otherwise apply under 102(a) or 102(b) as of publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the particular part of the reference relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: The particular part of the reference relied upon to support a rejection should be identified in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For clarity and proper record, point to the specific disclosure (paragraph, claim, figure) in the reference that supports anticipation or obviousness; follow form paragraph conventions for insertion and explanation.
